requirements.text: Patients should be able to book, cancel, or reschedule their appointments online without having to pick up the phone.
Patients should be able to request repeat prescriptions through the portal instead of calling in.
Patients should have secure online access to view their test results once a clinician has reviewed them.
The portal must be accessible for elderly patients or those who may not be comfortable with technology.
The system must have robust security measures in place to protect patient data privacy.
The appointment booking interface must show clear availability for both GP and nurse appointments.
Patients should receive confirmation notifications via their preferred method after booking an appointment.
Patients must be able to flag urgent symptoms to secure a same-day or emergency appointment.
The portal must have a secure login process for user authentication.
The solution must integrate seamlessly with existing practice management software.
The repeat prescription request interface must allow patients to view their current medications and request refills easily.
There must be a mechanism for clinicians to review repeat prescription requests before approval.
Patients must receive notifications confirming that their prescription request is being processed and when it is ready for pickup.
Patients should have access to their prescription history within the portal.
There should be a secure messaging feature for patients to communicate with clinicians regarding their prescription requests.
Patients should only view test results after a clinician has reviewed and authorized them.
Patients must receive notifications when their test results are available.
There should be a user-friendly dashboard for patients to navigate their test results.
Clinicians should be able to attach explanatory notes to test results when they are released.
Patients should have historical access to their past test results.
The portal should include educational resources related to common tests and their implications.
The portal must have a simple and intuitive design with a clean layout and clear navigation.
The portal should provide plain language instructions for each function.
Users should be able to adjust text size and contrast settings in the portal.
The portal should comply with accessibility standards, like WCAG 2.1 AA guidelines.
The portal should include video tutorials or help sections to assist users.
There should be a feedback mechanism for patients to provide input on their experience using the portal.
Support options, such as live chat or a dedicated help line, should be easily accessible in the portal.
The portal should allow family members to have proxy access to assist elderly patients.
